questions.name: back-and-resume-input
questions.question: Which selected pause commands reach an exact zero root request, and is physical B coverage established?
findings: Pause wrapper0x82DE5690 first calls common0x82E40680. Under current pause table0x82128F98, named OnAccept selects +0x30 ->0x82DE5670. That leaf supplies root0x8314F76C and exact r4=0, then current root+B0; matching root table0x82138768 selects0x82D7CE90.

Named OnCancel selects pause+0x34; initial common helper OnExit selects pause+0x18. Both initialized cells select0x821BC970, whose complete local body stores byte1 to H+8 and returns. They do not locally call the zero-request endpoint.
Initial helper0x82C7B710 recognizes OnInit/OnExit/PlaySound/StopSound; common0x82E40680 separately recognizes OnAccept/OnCancel/OnOption. No physical button producer was established.
Root0x82D7CE90 loads current C via U32[0x82FFD624]+0x70 and returns for null C. It selects C+0x10 for low8(r4)==0 and C+0xC otherwise. Exact zero is stronger than this byte test.
boundedNegatives: Defined-string FindStrings(OnBack,max8) emitted zero matches. This excludes only that defined-string model, not undefined/script/dynamic commands or physical B.
The complete selected completion-byte leaf has no local zero-request call. Later lifecycle resume is not excluded.
guards: Actual named command, valid H and current H vptr0x82128F98 at selection after earlier calls.
Comparison helper zero result, ordinary ABI preservation and normal helper return; helper0x827F27B0 and ABI targets unexpanded.
Current root vptr0x82138768, valid Q/current C and C current vptr/lifetime.
0x8314F10B, H+0x430 and child bytes+0x28/+0x29 retain presentation/input-meaning qualifications; they are not local guards in the zero leaf.
Outbound message delivery, received processing, current-state behavior and authority remain separate downstream boundaries.
unresolved: Physical B and visible Resume command production/current receiver; later completion/lifecycle resume; actual current root/state tables and downstream delivery.
questions.falsification: An actual physical B/Resume event delivers only OnCancel or OnExit to this retained table and completes without later exact-zero request; alternatively different live H/root tables defeat these cell joins.

questions.name: nonzero-opening
questions.question: Does the inverse request produce nonzero pause and does admitted processing request the pause child?
findings: Root nonzero-byte dispatch selects current C+0xC; matching key2 cell selects0x82E60C98. The producer builds matching message vptr0x8211EBA4/code17 with byte+0x34=1,+0x20=-1,+0x2C=1, and sends through nonnull current S+0x44 with third argument1.

Independently invoked process0x82D90C58 supplies b from message+0x34 and k from+0x20 to0x82E2A998. For b=1, old bit clear and admitted cache/gate conditions, consumer sets Q+4 bit0x800, mirrors the byte and invokes current frontend+B4 with k.

Matching root+B4 selects0x82D810E0: absent child requests0x434 bytes, constructs nonzero storage via0x82DE5740 and publishes it; an existing child receives k at+0x430. Both call0x82DE55D8 and its current H+0x8 entry request. Matching pause table selects accepted0x82C7BCC0 entry.
This is a conditional child-entry/presentation request. It does not join outbound send to received processing or prove rendered UI, focus, controller capture or gameplay pause.
guards: Valid matching current C/S/message/Q/frontend/child tables and retained storage/lifetimes, normal required returns and no disruptive alias/mutation.
Old bit must be clear. With gate byte nonzero, indexed cache T+4*k must be valid and differ from current turn; equality skips.
Allocation success and base-constructor return required for usable new child. Allocation-zero path still calls entry helper with zero and is not proved safe.
unresolved: Actual producer/processing invocation and peer delivery, message+0x20 source/range, current gate byte and cache, successful registration/render/input ownership.
questions.falsification: Already-set bit, equal cache turn, missing actual invocation, different live table, allocation failure or lost object/state retention prevents the selected effect.

findings: Newly identified complete factory0x821D3D78 requests0x38 bytes. Nonzero allocation initializes matching vptr0x8211EBA4, code17,+0x20=-1,+0x2C=1 and byte+0x34=0, then returns the object. Null allocation returns0. No incoming discriminator/buffer is consumed locally.

A fresh exact aligned pointer scan emitted one cell0x8216CC58 selecting that factory, with descriptor0x40002803 at0x8216CC5C. The row lies inside accepted executable function-pointer/descriptor metadata [0x8216B800,0x8218A050); it is not evidence of a network factory registry.

Matching message+0x10 selects0x82D90C58, which calls0x82E2A998 and returns1 on normal return. Neither the factory address nor that return establishes actual received-object selection, deserialization, processing invocation or successful pause change.

Actual message+0x20 producer. The accepted selected base-envelope read/write sequences omit+0x20; its default -1 is not a received index identity or a proved peer ID.

questions.name: sender-self-peer-and-acknowledgement
questions.question: Is own processing synchronous/queued/looped back or peer-gated, and what do selected sender gates prove?
findings: Selected sender0x82CA6500 can return for null info getter or S+0x14. Admitted work serializes and visits indices0..7, gated by a nonnull first map lookup. Eight is a fixed index capacity here, not a proved active-peer count.

Per-index helper0x82E465F8 receives X=U32[S+0x38] through the selected S+0x118 getter, then uses registry key U32[X+0x2C], nonnull returned J and nonzero low byte from unexpanded0x82E46518(X,index value). It then reaches current J virtual+0x80 at0x82E46684. Failure returns original index; success locally preserves virtual return, subject to ABI/return premises.
Sender uses that result for a second map lookup, dereferencing result+0x14 without a new local null check; the first and second records need not be the same.

Forwarder0x82CA4530 uses a count-driven loop and current P=U32[S+0x14] virtual+0xC at0x82CA45A8. It does not locally wait or branch on send acknowledgement/result. Transitive transport behavior is unbound.
Selected S+0x128 target0x822E2770 only returns float[S+0x44]; the sender stores f1 to first-record+8. This is not an acknowledgement check or proved timestamp semantics.

Selected local sender words contain no direct message virtual+0x10/process/consumer call. J+0x80, P+0xC and other callbacks can still provide synchronous local, queued, loopback or remote processing. No route is selected without current identities/targets.
guards: Current S table must match selected cells; info/registry/map/buffer records must be valid and retained across normally returning helpers. No arbitrary registry or transport target chosen by shape.
unresolved: Current J key/vptr/+0x80 and P/vptr/+0xC target/effects, actual self-index mapping, receive invocation, peer requirements and authority.
rejectedInterpretations: Selected +0x128 as an acknowledgement or peer-count gate.
Factory metadata pointer as proof of network receive selection.
questions.falsification: Matching current J/P targets and retained invocation dataflow to process0x82D90C58, self-key mapping and delivery order would decide the synchronous/queued/loopback alternatives.
questions.deliveryBoundary: Current selector and transport virtual targets, self-record identity and received processing invocation remain unbound. Sender-local words establish neither synchronous self processing nor an acknowledgement or participant-exclusion gate.

questions.name: duplicate-race-and-authority
questions.question: What repeat, later-pause, race and authority guarantees follow from the selected consumer?
findings: For native-producer bytes0/1, consumer returns when sampled Q+4 bit0x800 already equals b. A serialized second zero after a completed clear, with same valid Q and no intervening mutation, skips bit/mirror stores and frontend callback.

Zero bypasses the indexed current-turn cache. A later nonzero after clear can set the bit again when initial mismatch and current gate/cache admit it; gate-nonzero same k/current-turn equality instead skips.

Zero has no local age/sequence rejection. A prior zero delivered after a newer admitted pause can clear it. The same-state early return occurs before cache recording, so universal suppression of reordered older pauses is not proved.

Separate load/compare/store and subsequent callbacks do not establish concurrency or exactly-once safety. Concurrent zeros may both admit; other bit updates may race. External serialization can exclude these interleavings but is not established here.

Selected zero arm has no explicit host/peer identity test. Ingress, selector, transport, receive dispatch and callbacks can still enforce authority. Any-participant global resume is not proved by this local absence.
guards: Serialized completed calls, same valid Q/storage and no intervening mutation are required for duplicate-zero skip. Actual b/k/T, gate source, current turn, callback identity and effects remain conditional.
unresolved: Actual external serialization/order, message+0x20 identity and index capacity/reset, current gate-byte key/registry/+0x94 source, host/participant authority and retained frontend effects.
questions.falsification: An intervening admitted nonzero or overlapping consumer calls invalidates the no-intervening-mutation duplicate premise. Independent current-target/order/authority evidence could establish stronger guarantees.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only Ghidra queries, exact supported-image word comparison and fixed-four-byte PowerPC decoding. Truncated decompiler output does not establish a complete native body. ABI and helper returns remain premises; mapped thunk bytes at 0x827F3F50..0x827F4280 are excluded.

remaining: Actual B/Resume ingress, received selection/processing invocation, current dynamic transport/selector targets, +0x20 index provenance, external ordering/authority and retained global resume remain unbound.
falsification: Different instruction words or live table/receiver identities invalidate the corresponding selected route. An exact physical-input producer, received factory-selection and processing call, or current transport target can resolve the bounded alternatives; address proximity and metadata pointers alone cannot.
conclusion: The selected named OnAccept route supplies an exact zero request; OnCancel and OnExit select a completion-byte leaf instead. Physical B and visible Resume delivery remain unbound. Admitted nonzero processing sets pause and requests the child. A matching message factory is identified without received selection or process invocation. A serialized duplicate zero skips after a completed clear, while later nonzero and older zero requests retain ordering risks. Current selector, transport and authority joins remain unresolved.
